title: Sofacy_Fysbis_Backdoor_Investigation_54a
description: You are an incident responder tasked with investigating a potential compromise involving the Sofacy group's Fysbis backdoor on a Linux-based network. The Fysbis malware is known for its modular capabilities, including command-and-control (C2) communication, exfiltration, and persistence mechanisms. Your goal is to identify and mitigate the threat.
outcomes: Identify and investigate suspicious services and processes.
Determine persistence mechanisms and lateral movement techniques.
Collect and analyze forensic evidence to understand the scope of the compromise.

levels.title: Introduction
levels.content: You are an incident responder tasked with investigating a potential compromise involving the Sofacy group's Fysbis backdoor on a Linux-based network. The Fysbis malware is known for its modular capabilities, including command-and-control (C2) communication, exfiltration, and persistence mechanisms. Your goal is to identify and mitigate the threat.

levels.title: Get Access
levels.cloud_content: Access the target host via SSH using the following credentials: Username: cyrano, Password: cyrano. Enter 'start' to begin.
levels.local_content: Access the target host via SSH using the following credentials: Username: cyrano, Password: cyrano. Enter 'start' to begin.

levels.title: Suspicious Service Discovery
levels.content: While monitoring the network, you noticed unusual outbound connections from the `target` host. Investigate the host to identify any unauthorized or suspicious services running on the system.
levels.solution: To identify the suspicious service, you can use the `systemctl list-units --type=service` command to list all running services. Look for any services that seem out of place or unfamiliar. The suspicious service in this scenario is the `bkd.service`.

hints.title: First hint title
hints.content: Check the list of running services and look for any that seem out of place or unfamiliar.

hints.title: Second hint title
hints.content: Use the `systemctl list-units --type=service` command to list all running services.

hints.title: Third hint title
hints.content: The suspicious service is not a standard system service. Look for services with unusual names or descriptions.

levels.title: Persistence Discovery
levels.content: Now that you have identified the suspicious service, determine how it is automatically started after a system reboot. This will help you understand the persistence mechanism used by the attacker.
levels.solution: To determine the persistence mechanism, you can use the `systemctl list-unit-files` command to list all systemd unit files. Look for any unit files related to the suspicious service. The persistence mechanism in this scenario is the `bkd.service` unit file.

hints.title: First hint title
hints.content: Investigate systemd services and timers to find any related to the suspicious service.

hints.title: Second hint title
hints.content: Use the `systemctl list-unit-files` command to list all systemd unit files.

hints.title: Third hint title
hints.content: The persistence mechanism is likely a systemd service or timer. Look for any unit files related to the suspicious service.

levels.title: Lateral Movement Investigation
levels.content: Examine the `target` host for evidence of lateral movement. Identify any file transfers or remote execution techniques used to move between hosts within the network.
levels.solution: To investigate lateral movement, you can check system logs and network connections for any unusual activity involving the `next-target` host. The service or script responsible for lateral movement in this scenario is the `payload-transfer.service`.

hints.title: First hint title
hints.content: Check system logs and network connections for any unusual activity involving the `next-target` host.

hints.title: Second hint title
hints.content: Use the `journalctl -u payload-transfer.service` command to check the logs of the payload-transfer service.

hints.title: Third hint title
hints.content: The lateral movement mechanism is likely a service or script that transfers files or executes commands remotely. Look for any services or scripts related to file transfers or remote execution.
